subject: [RFC PATCH 3/5] mm/page_alloc: convert any movable pageblock on a non-movable allocation

2026-10-07.patch_summary: This patch modifies the behavior of try_to_claim_block() in the Linux kernel's page allocation system. It ensures that a movable block is converted to match the type of non-movable allocation it serves, even if only half its pages are free or compatible. This change aims to prevent non-movable content from being stored in blocks typed as movable. The patch also introduces stricter rules for converting non-movable pageblocks to movable, requiring every page to be free or movable before a movable claim can take the block. Additionally, it ensures that blocks straddling zone edges are never claimed and modifies the behavior of zone_spans_pageblock() to test whether a block lies wholly inside its zone.

reviews.author: Johannes Weiner
reviews.summary: The reviewer is concerned that the patch may lead to an explosion of non-movable pageblocks if short-lived unmovable allocations are made frequently, making it hard to recover when the bar for claiming movable blocks is raised.
reviews.raw_body:
I like this in theory, but wonder how this behaves in practice.

The block is claimed, but the movable constituents aren't proactively
kicked out. The next unmovable request might well claim another mostly
movable block, and so forth. With a flurry of short-lived unmovable
allocations, this might explode the unmovable blocks, which will be
hard to recover especially when you raise the bar on *that* direction.

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary: Author is addressing a concern about splitting up the patch series, offering to resend it in smaller portions as separate patches.
sentiment_signals: author is willing to accommodate reviewer's preference
patch author is open to revising the submission process
reviews.raw_body:
I have code for that, too, but it seems like
it's a lot easier to get things reviewed in
small portions.

If you want I can resend this as a larger
series, with:
1) the pageblock claiming
2) per migrate type free lists
3) evacuation of movable pages from unmovable 
   pageblocks, when the kernel free lists fall 
   below a watermark

That would be the full extent of the 2MB granularity
fragmentation avoidance stuff I have here.

Just let me know your preference.

-- 
All Rights Reversed.

2026-10-14.patch_summary: This patch modifies the behavior of try_to_claim_block() to convert any movable pageblock on a non-movable allocation, regardless of how many pages are free or compatible. This ensures that the block's type matches the allocation it serves and prevents non-movable content from being stored in movable-typed blocks. The patch also introduces stricter rules for converting non-movable pageblocks to movable, requiring all pages to be free or movable before claiming a block. Additionally, blocks straddling zone edges are never claimed due to their potential for inconsistent behavior.

reviews.author: Dev Jain
reviews.summary: Reviewer Dev Jain noted that the patch series as-is would regress performance by having many unmovable pageblocks with movable allocations, which could hurt memory-transparent huge pages (mTHP) allocations.
reviews.raw_body:
I think your patch series applied as-is would regress stuff:
we may have lots of UNMOVABLE pageblocks with lots of
movable allocations, unable to be rescued, hurting mTHP
allocations.

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary: Author is seeking feedback on how to proceed with the patch series, asking reviewers whether they want to review each patch individually before an update or post the entire series at once.
reviews.raw_body:
How should we move forward with this?

Do do guys want to review this series first,
and then I post an update with the other
stuff, before any gets merged?

Or do you want me to post a larger series
all at once?

Before I move on, do the combined policy
changes from patches 3, 4, and 5 make sense
to you (with or without evacuation) ?

Patch 1 from this series can be merged all
by itself as a separate thing.

-- 
All Rights Reversed.
